+==============================================================================+
|                                                                              |
|   PHYSICAL          CHEMICAL          GEOLOGICAL         BIOLOGICAL          |
|   OCEANOGRAPHY      OCEANOGRAPHY      OCEANOGRAPHY       OCEANOGRAPHY        |
|   ───────────       ────────────      ────────────       ────────────        |
|   Heat transport    Seawater chem     Seafloor morph     Marine ecology      |
|   Currents/gyres    Carbonate system  Plate tectonics    Food webs           |
|   Stratification    Nutrient cycles   Sediment records   Microbial loops     |
|   Waves/tides       Trace metals      Hydrothermal       Deep sea biology    |
|   Sound channels    Ocean acidif.     vents/seeps        Fisheries science   |
+==============================================================================+
|                                                                              |
|   OCEAN BASINS (5)                          DEPTH PROVINCES                  |
|   ─────────────                             ────────────────                 |
|   Pacific  165M km²  deepest mean          Epipelagic     0–200 m            |
|   Atlantic  82M km²  saltiest              Mesopelagic    200–1,000 m        |
|   Indian    73M km²  warmest mean          Bathypelagic   1,000–4,000 m      |
|   Southern  21M km²  stormiest             Abyssopelagic  4,000–6,000 m      |
|   Arctic    14M km²  shallowest mean       Hadalpelagic   6,000–11,000 m     |
|                                                                              |
+==============================================================================+
|  Global mean depth: 3,688 m     Max depth: 10,935 m (Challenger Deep)       |
|  Volume: 1.335 billion km³      Mean salinity: ~35 PSU                       |
|  Thermohaline residence time: ~1,000–2,000 yr                                |
+==============================================================================+

SHELF       SLOPE         RISE        ABYSSAL PLAIN     MID-OCEAN RIDGE
 0─200 m    200─2000 m   2000─4000 m    4000─6000 m       varies
┌──────────┐
│Continental│\
│  Crust   │  \                                         /──────────────\
│ (~35 km) │    \───────────────────────────────────────  Ridge Crest  │
└──────────┘     Submarine canyons cut the slope         Rift Valley  │
                  Turbidite flows carry sediment down                   └──

MORPHOLOGICAL FEATURES:
  Continental shelf    <200 m, <0.1° slope — geologically part of continent
  Continental slope    200–2000 m, 1–4° slope, cut by submarine canyons
  Continental rise     sediment apron at base of slope (turbidite lobes)
  Abyssal plain        flattest terrain on Earth, 4–6 km depth
  Mid-ocean ridge      60,000 km global chain, seafloor spreading center
  Trench               subduction margins, deepest zones up to 11 km
  Seamount             isolated volcanic peak >1000 m above seafloor
  Guyot                flat-topped seamount (wave-planed when at surface)
  Fracture zone        transform fault scar offsetting ridge segments

blocks.heading_context: ## Ocean Provinces by Depth and Light
blocks.text:
SURFACE ─────── 0 m
   EPIPELAGIC (sunlit zone)        0–200 m    Photosynthesis possible
─────────────── ~200 m
   MESOPELAGIC (twilight zone)     200–1000 m  Dim light; vertical migration
─────────────── 1000 m
   BATHYPELAGIC (midnight zone)    1–4 km      No light; permanent darkness
─────────────── 4000 m
   ABYSSOPELAGIC                   4–6 km      Near-freezing; high pressure
─────────────── 6000 m
   HADALPELAGIC (hadal zone)       >6 km       Only in trenches
─────────────── 10,935 m CHALLENGER DEEP

BENTHIC ZONES (seafloor equivalents):
  Sublittoral     shelf seafloor
  Bathyal         slope seafloor
  Abyssal         abyssal plain seafloor
  Hadal           trench floor
